dedupe_keys.name: blackett review satellite derived time and position a study of critical dependencies uk 2018

description: This national risk and vulnerability assessment, a Blackett review published in January 2018 by the UK Government Office for Science under the Government Chief Scientific Adviser Sir Mark Walport, examined how far British critical services depend on time and position from satellite navigation systems and how exposed they are to disruption. It found that resilience needed to improve across all critical services and recommended that operators of critical national infrastructure review and report their reliance on GNSS, that the Cabinet Office assess overall national dependence, that spectrum be protected against interference, that government set up a formal internal advice system on positioning and timing, that backup systems be deployed where appropriate, and that skills, future technologies and common terminology be addressed. Its findings fed into later policy, including the 2023 UK positioning, navigation and timing policy framework. Coverage: United Kingdom, all critical sectors that use satellite time or position, as of 2017. Format and access: free PDF on GOV.UK. Caveats: the review is qualitative and does not quantify losses; implementation was slow, as later commentary noted. Simulation uses: mapping cascading dependencies of energy, telecom, finance and transport on GNSS timing, defining hazard scenarios of jamming, spoofing and space weather, and resilience planning for backups. Related records: the London Economics studies put costs on the same scenarios, and the UK PNT policy framework of 2023 is the policy response.
